newsitem.title: USA: Consumer group sets off heating oil alarm.
newsitem.headline: Consumer group sets off heating oil alarm.

text.p: Consumer advocates Citizen Action on Tuesday urged the U.S. Energy Department to step into oil markets to prevent a steep climb in heating oil prices this winter.

With heating oil stocks at the end of August at 109 million barrels, down from 131 million barrels at the same time last year and 139 million barrels the previous year, the market was poised to skyrocket, warned Citizen Action's energy policy director Edwin Rothschild.

"These extraordinarily low stock levels combined with higher demand for distillate fuels will lead to sharp price increases for homeowners and the trucking industry if nothing is done to increase production," he said.

The northeastern states were most vulnerable, Rothschild said, because heating oil stocks on the East Coast at 21 million barrels were at half the level seen a year ago, according to government statistics.
Rothschild said unless oil companies built inventories up to 140 million barrels over the next two months, prices could rise by as much as 20 cents a gallon.

"Because refiners are unlikely to build sufficient supplies of home heating oil, especially in the Northeast, we are calling on the Secretary of Energy to use the Strategic Petroleum Reserve in tandem with the futures market to make more heating oil supplies available," he said.
The Energy Department had no immediate comment on Citizen Action's proposal.
